findings.statement: Top convergence gene. PMID:42473996 reports CA9 preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumour cells with low background in normal kidney, and CA9-targeted PET as proof-of-concept for noninvasive ccRCC discrimination, 'warranting prospective validation' (single early study). High CA9 PET uptake was linked to PBRM1 loss-of-function. Clinical-stage anti-CA9 drugs exist (girentuximab, phase 3, per Open Targets). Caveat: TCGA Cox shows no prognostic signal and DepMap shows no dependency, so CA9 is a diagnostic/imaging/delivery target, not a prognostic marker or functional dependency.

PMID:38195301: CD70 is commonly overexpressed in RCC, minimally expressed in normal tissue, a potential therapeutic target for advanced RCC; in ccRCC it correlates with hypoxia pathway proteins (HIF downstream target). PMID:39510586: high and specific CD70 expression makes it a diagnostic and therapeutic target; 68Ga single-domain antibody radiotracers (RCCB3, RCCB6) were developed; CD70 expression associated with overall survival. Preclinical/early clinical-stage evidence, consistent with data (tumour-intrinsic, strong TCGA up-regulation). TCGA Cox does not show prognostic value, so the survival association is not replicated by the data.

NDUFA4L2 (COXFA4L2) is the best-documented mechanistic ccRCC gene in the corpus. HIF-1alpha induces its expression and mitochondrial localisation (PMID:42331208); the large majority of ccRCCs overexpress it and it increases glycolysis (PMID:36722045); it suppresses mitochondria-associated ferroptosis cooperatively with LDHB, with the NDUFA4L2/LDHB axis proposed as a therapeutic strategy (PMID:42331208); it is predictive of poor survival and supports proliferation in cell lines (PMID:34970493), and is a tissue/EV marker for low- and high-grade ccRCC (PMID:41656939). Preclinical only, no approved drug. Caveat: TCGA Cox in this graph does not show prognostic value, and DepMap shows no selective dependency, so the poor-survival claim and the target claim are not supported by the data profiles.

PMID:41399267: NNMT up-regulated in ccRCC tumour tissue; high NNMT correlated with worse overall and disease-specific survival, and the authors call it a promising prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target (transcriptomic, clinical and functional validation). PMID:37523719 describes selective NNMT inhibitors (II559, II802) with high reported selectivity over related methyltransferases, so a pharmacological route exists. This is one of few genes where literature and TCGA agree on adverse prognosis (Cox significant), and it has high biomarker profile score; however, DepMap does not show selective dependency.

Down-regulated in ccRCC (IHC lower than adjacent normal, PMID:40852386); described as prognostic biomarker and potential immunotherapy target, linked to Treg, Th17 and neutrophil infiltration; PMID:38655323 calls it an independent predictor of prognosis in KIRC. Evidence is bioinformatic plus IHC in one cohort. Data agree on loss and favourable prognosis (TCGA Cox significant), but loss of expression makes it a poor direct therapeutic target (target profile low); the 'immunotherapy target' claim is not supported by data.

PMID:38335255 identifies HILPDA as key driver of MYC-driven lipid droplet accumulation (proliferation, LD formation and tumour growth impaired on downregulation) and a specific ccRCC biomarker versus healthy kidney. PMID:41399267 reports it up-regulated in tumour but with no prognostic impact, consistent with TCGA Cox showing none. Diagnostic marker/mechanism, not prognostic; no drugs.

PMID:37760940: ENO2 is a potential diagnostic biomarker that independently predicts prognosis and promotes ccRCC progression via glycolysis (Warburg effect). PMID:39091581: ENO2 interference inhibits glycolysis, promotes ferroptosis and affects mitochondrial function in ccRCC cell lines. PMID:36313709 lists it among genes related to OS. Consistent with TCGA (up, adverse Cox), but in vitro/bioinformatic only and no DepMap dependency; NSE data in PMID:34467977 concern intraocular metastasis in RCC generally, not ccRCC specifically.

Contradictory literature direction. PMID:36204178: MT1G down-regulated in ccRCC versus normal and 'may be a negative regulator of ferroptosis ... and a biomarker of poor prognosis'. PMID:38906969: low in tumours, yet high MT1G correlates with advanced stage and poorer prognosis, and elevated MT1G promotes growth and metastasis by inhibiting CPT1B (H3K14 trimethylation) and lipid droplet accumulation. PMID:40247376: SAP30 inhibits MT1G, impairing zinc delivery to p53. Thus MT1G is lost in tumour but harmful when high; TCGA Cox adverse supports the latter. A tumour-suppressor versus oncogenic role is unresolved.

Contradictory direction. PMID:41158242 (pan-cancer analysis): ABAT underexpressed in KIRC yet 'predicted poor prognosis in KIRC'. PMID:41813748: ABAT overexpression suppresses tumour growth in vitro and in vivo via cGAS-STING and PRMT5, enhancing interferon signalling. TCGA Cox in the graph shows lower ABAT hazard (favourable high expression), so the pan-cancer poor-prognosis sentence conflicts with the data. Vigabatrin (ABAT inhibitor, phase 4) would be counter-productive if ABAT is tumour-suppressive.

PMID:36123895: SLC22A8 protein, phosphorylation and DNA methylation lower in ccRCC than normal; expression correlated with survival and immune infiltration and proposed as prognostic biomarker. Single bioinformatic study; consistent with strong loss and favourable Cox in TCGA, but loss of a transporter is a marker, not a druggable target.

Literature gap: SCARB1 ranks high on omics (tumour-up, purity-robust), Open Targets genetic association and the target profile, but has no literature relations in this corpus; a sentence search returned only generic ccRCC sentences. It is a data-driven candidate with no literature validation in this corpus and should be flagged as a hypothesis.

caveats: Corpus is about 320 ccRCC abstracts; most gene claims come from one or two papers, often bioinformatic (TCGA-based) analyses, so literature agreement partly re-uses the same TCGA data as the omics streams (not independent).

Prognostic claims for CA9, CD70 and NDUFA4L2 in the literature are not mirrored by TCGA Cox results in this graph; DepMap shows no selective dependency for the top candidates, so target status rests on expression selectivity and tractability, not functional essentiality.
UMOD, FABP1 and NPHS2 have literature relations but were not reviewed in detail; kidney-normal genes lost in tumour are better biomarkers than targets.
Findings quote extracted relations; the PubMed connector was not authorised in this session so no external literature was consulted.
